issues.description: Field identifier mismatch in Lecture class: the problem statement UML and textual description specify camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares private fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor and methods in the same solution file use the camelCase identifiers (e.g., this.lectureName). This intra-file naming discrepancy causes compilation errors (undefined symbol references) and prevents students from mapping the UML-specified attributes to the implemented fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute identifiers consistent across artifacts and within the solution. Prefer renaming the declared fields in the solution to the camelCase names used in the UML and by the constructor/methods: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Alternatively, update the constructor and all methods to use the snake_case field names, but aligning to the UML/camelCase is recommended so students can directly map requirements to code.
